content.doc_md:
## Tutorials

The INSTR() function returns the position of the first occurrence of a string 
in another string.

This function performs a case-insensitive search.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT INSTR("W3Schools.com", "3") AS MatchPosition;

---

INSTR(
string1
,
string2
)

---

SELECT INSTR("W3Schools.com", "COM") AS MatchPosition;

---

SELECT INSTR(CustomerName, "a")
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The LCASE() function converts a string to lower-case.

Note:TheLOWER()function is a synonym for the LCASE() 
function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT LCASE("SQL Tutorial is FUN!");

---

LCASE(
text
)

---

SELECT LCASE(CustomerName) AS LowercaseCustomerName
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The LEFT() function extracts a number of characters from a string (starting from left).

Tip:Also look at theRIGHT()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT LEFT("SQL Tutorial", 3) AS ExtractString;

---

LEFT(
string
,
number_of_chars
)

---

SELECT LEFT(CustomerName, 5) AS ExtractString
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The LENGTH() function returns the length of a string (in bytes).

### Code Examples

```
SELECT LENGTH("SQL Tutorial") AS LengthOfString;

---

LENGTH(
string
)

---

SELECT LENGTH(CustomerName) AS LengthOfName
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The LOCATE() function returns the position of the first occurrence of a substring in a string.

If the substring is not found within the original string, this function returns 0.

This function performs a case-insensitive search.

Note:This function is equal to thePOSITION()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT LOCATE("3", "W3Schools.com") AS MatchPosition;

---

LOCATE(
substring
,
string
,
start
)

---

SELECT LOCATE("com", "W3Schools.com", 3) AS MatchPosition;

---

SELECT LOCATE("a", CustomerName)
FROM Customers;
```
